findings.issue_text: [BUG] POLICY_SOME_HTML only permits br, p, strong, and b, so the verifier reports 'Illegal HTML' for every key in the English source files themselves that use any other tag (em, ul, li, span, code, h1, etc.), because the en-file check compares the raw value (still containing e.g. <em>) against its own sanitized output with that tag stripped. The first full run of the theme-verifier over the themes/js message bundles fails the build on the English source files — keys like terms/otp texts that use tags outside the four whitelisted ones are self-flagged, making the new check impossible to pass without mass message edits that this diff does not contain.

[BUG] The Lithuanian totpStep1 was replaced with Italian text 'Installa una delle seguenti applicazioni sul tuo cellulare:' (copy-pasted from the Italian file), not a Lithuanian translation. Lithuanian users of the account console see an Italian sentence on the TOTP setup page after this change ships.

[ADVISORY] The Simplified-Chinese file's totpStep1 was replaced with Traditional-Chinese characters ('在您的手機上安裝以下應用程式之一：' uses 手機/應用程式 rather than 手机/应用程式). zh_CN users see mixed-script text on the TOTP setup page; anyone re-touching this line has to notice the script mismatch before the fix.

[BUG] santizeAnchors advances englishMatcher once per anchor found in the translation, so when a translation legitimately repeats an anchor that appears once in the English string, the second occurrence triggers 'Didn't find anchor tag ... in original string' because englishMatcher.find() returns false. Any translated message with a repeated (identical) link against a single-link English source — a valid translation pattern — fails verification with a false-positive error, blocking legitimate community translations.

[ADVISORY] The English reference file path is derived by string replaceAll("resources-community", "resources") plus a suffix regex, so any English file living anywhere other than the exact mirrored product path (e.g. bundles without a product counterpart or a path containing 'resources-community' as substring elsewhere) resolves to a nonexistent file and verifySafeHtml throws a raw RuntimeException instead of a MojoExecutionException. The next contributor who adds a locale file in a directory layout that does not literally mirror 'resources-community' → 'resources' gets an unhandled RuntimeException in the Maven plugin (stack trace, not the plugin's error contract), and has to reverse-engineer the undocumented path-mirroring assumption.

[ADVISORY] No test in the diff exercises the normalizeValue branches (templateHelp/optimizeLookupHelp/choice-format stripping, the email RTL style strip, or the entity-unescape round-trip), even though those branches are the load-bearing escape hatches that keep real Keycloak bundles passing. A regression in normalizeValue (e.g. the choice-format regex stopping to match {2,choice,...} after a message-format change like the one in this very diff) silently turns into a wall of 'Illegal HTML' failures across all locale files at the next CI run, with no test pinpointing the cause.

[BUG] The rewritten error-invalid-multivalued-size uses Java MessageFormat choice syntax ({2,choice,0#values|1#value|1<values}) in files consumed by the JS admin UI, with no verification anywhere in the diff that the JS-side message formatter supports choice patterns. The React admin console (and account UI) format server error keys with a placeholder-substitution formatter, not Java MessageFormat; users see the literal string '{2,choice,0#values|1#value|1<values}' (or an un-substituted '{2}') in the validation error toast instead of 'value(s)'.

[BUG] error-invalid-multivalued-size in the account UI messages bundle was switched from {{0}}-style placeholders to MessageFormat choice syntax with no test or renderer check covering it. Account-console users with multivalued-attribute validation failures get a garbled or un-interpolated error message; the diff contains no test that any JS renderer resolves {2,choice,...}.

[BUG] verifySafeHtml resolves the English bundle by string-replacing the absolute path and throws a raw RuntimeException when the English file is absent, instead of recording a verification message via the messages list. When any theme directory contains a locale properties file whose _en sibling does not exist (e.g. a locale file added to resources-community without a matching resources _en file, or any path where the regex '_[a-zA-Z-_]*\\.properties' does not match, such as a locale containing digits), the Maven plugin crashes with 'unable to read file' instead of reporting a proper verification failure, breaking the build with an unattributable stack trace.

[BUG] The English-file path is derived via replaceAll("resources-community", "resources") and the locale regex on the absolute path, and this path-mapping heuristic itself is never verified — if the mapping ever points at a nonexistent or wrong file there is no sanity check, and the regex '_[a-zA-Z-_]*\\.properties' silently fails for locale suffixes containing digits (e.g. es_419). A locale code with digits leaves the path un-rewritten so the verifier reads the non-English file as its own 'English' source, silently skipping the HTML comparison instead of verifying it.

[BUG] normalizeValue hard-codes a whitelist of exemptions (templateHelp, optimizeLookupHelp, linkExpirationFormatter.timePeriodUnit*, error-invalid-multivalued-size) so any other key using MessageFormat choice patterns or angle-bracket text fails verification with a false 'Illegal HTML' report. The next contributor adding a choice-format or angle-bracket message key (the pattern this very diff introduces for error-invalid-multivalued-size) gets a failing theme-verifier build and must discover this hidden exemption list to fix it; no test documents the requirement.

[ADVISORY] The test suite only covers the negative cases (illegal HTML, no-HTML, changed anchor, duplicate keys); there is no test that a valid translated file with legitimate HTML and anchors passes with an empty messages list, and no test for the missing-English-file or RTL-email paths. False-positive regressions in the sanitizer comparison (e.g. the '<!-- -->' stripping, unescapeHtml4 round-trip, or anchor-removal leaving text) will not be caught, breaking every downstream i18n PR that adds a legitimate translation.

[BUG] The Lithuanian totpStep1 replacement inserts Italian text ('Installa una delle seguenti applicazioni sul tuo cellulare:') into the Lithuanian bundle. Lithuanian users see an Italian sentence in the TOTP setup page — the HTML-sanitization rewrite silently replaced content with the wrong language instead of a sanitized Lithuanian translation.

[BUG] The Simplified-Chinese (zh_CN) totpStep1 was replaced with Traditional Chinese text ('在您的手機上安裝以下應用程式之一：') while the file is the Simplified bundle. Simplified-Chinese users get Traditional characters in the account TOTP page; the diff also drops the FreeOTP/Google Play links the English source still carries, so the 'install one of the following applications' sentence is followed by no list of applications.

[BUG] The Lithuanian totpStep1 is replaced with Italian text 'Installa una delle seguenti applicazioni sul tuo cellulare:', corrupting the lt translation with a wrong-language string. Lithuanian users see an Italian sentence on the account TOTP setup page; this content change is not traceable to the sanitizer requirement and ships broken translation.

[BUG] The Simplified-Chinese totpStep1 is replaced with Traditional Chinese text '在您的手機上安裝以下應用程式之一：' (手機/應用程式), mismatching the file's zh-CN locale. zh-CN users get a wrong-variant sentence on the account TOTP page; a wrong-locale string entered the file under the guise of sanitizer-driven fixes.

[ADVISORY] santizeAnchors only validates anchors present in the translation against the English source; a translation that drops anchors entirely (as the fi/lt/sk/sv/zh totpStep1 edits in this very PR do, leaving 'install one of the following applications:' with no list or links) passes verification, so the 'translation preserves source anchors' invariant is only enforced in one direction. Translators can silently strip required links and informational content from user-facing messages and CI stays green; the next reviewer cannot rely on the verifier to catch content loss.

[BUG] verifySafeHtml throws a raw RuntimeException when the derived English sibling file cannot be read, instead of adding to the `messages` result list or throwing MojoExecutionException, so a properties file without an _en.properties counterpart (e.g. a community file whose English original lives only in the main resources tree the replaceAll does not reach, or a file named outside the `_[a-zA-Z-_]*\.properties` pattern) crashes the build with an unhandled stack trace. Any new locale file added without a matching _en sibling in the expected path breaks the verifier build with an opaque RuntimeException rather than a reportable verification message, and the verify() contract (returning messages) is silently abandoned on that path.

[ADVISORY] Changing error-invalid-multivalued-size from '{{0}}...{{2}} value(s)' to ICU MessageFormat choice syntax '{0}...{2,choice,0#values|1#value|1<values}' alters the runtime message-format semantics of this key, which is not traceable to the PR's stated intent (adding a sanitizer to the theme verifier). If either JS UI renders this key without ICU MessageFormat support, users see the literal '{2,choice,0#values|1#value|1<values}' string in the attribute-validation error; this behavior change ships under a sanitizer-titled PR where it escapes review by rendering experts.

[ADVISORY] The verifier adds the owasp-java-html-sanitizer and commons-text dependencies with hard-pinned versions and no scope alignment (owasp is compile-scope though it is only used by the verification logic, commons-text gets an explicit compile scope), expanding the module's dependency surface beyond what the requirements touch. Future Keycloak dependency-management bumps of these artifacts will not reach this module, so the security-sensitive sanitizer version silently diverges; maintainers get version-drift audit noise on every OWASP/commons-text CVE advisory.

[BUG] The Lithuanian totpStep1 translation was replaced with Italian text ('Installa una delle seguenti applicazioni sul tuo cellulare:') instead of a Lithuanian translation. Lithuanian users see Italian text on the TOTP setup page; the sanitizer fix was used as cover for a wrong-language paste and nothing in the verifier catches it, so it ships.

[BUG] The Simplified-Chinese totpStep1 was replaced with Traditional Chinese ('在您的手機上安裝以下應用程式之一：') rather than Simplified. Simplified-Chinese users get Traditional characters, and the diff proves the replacement pipeline is copy-paste from unrelated locales with no verification of language match.

[BUG] verifySafeHtml re-opens the file and constructs the English-file path by string-munging (replaceAll of 'resources-community' and a locale regex), and throws a bare RuntimeException on IOException, which escapes verify()'s try/catch (it only catches IOException) and crashes the Mojo. Any properties file whose English sibling is not at the derived path (e.g. a theme whose English file lives elsewhere, or a new community-only theme) aborts the entire verifier build with a raw RuntimeException stack trace instead of a reported per-file message; the path-derivation heuristic is a parallel hand-maintained mapping that breaks silently whenever the directory layout changes.

[ADVISORY] santizeAnchors enforces anchor equality in document order, so a translation that legitimately reorders two anchors relative to the English source (e.g. swaps two links in a sentence) fails the check even though the anchor set is identical. Translators of the ~40 locale files this PR touches get hard build failures for semantically-correct reorderings, and the 'fix' is to contort the sentence to English word order.

[ADVISORY] normalizeValue keeps a hand-maintained per-key exception list (templateHelp, optimizeLookupHelp, choice patterns) that must grow by one entry for every future message key containing literal angle-bracket text, and containsHtml's regex `<[a-z]+[^>]*>` misclassifies such literals as HTML. The next contributor who adds a message key with a literal `<NAME>`-style placeholder gets a spurious 'Illegal HTML' build failure (or an over-permissive SOME_HTML policy, since the English literal triggers containsHtml), and must discover and extend this private allowlist — a parallel enumeration with no single source of truth.

[ADVISORY] The English-file path is derived with replaceAll("_[a-zA-Z-_]*\\.properties", "_en.properties"), a regex applied to the whole absolute path where the first match may not be the filename segment if any directory name matches the pattern. A theme directory named like `*_xx.properties` (or a future rename of the messages directory) silently resolves the English bundle to a nonexistent or wrong file, which then surfaces as the RuntimeException crash in the adjacent lookup rather than a clear configuration error.

[ADVISORY] When an anchor mismatch is found, santizeAnchors reports and breaks but still returns the value with the mismatching anchor unstripped, so the subsequent sanitize step emits a second, differently-worded 'Illegal HTML' message for the same key. CI output shows two contradictory diagnoses for one defect, and the test fixture only asserts on the first message wording, so the duplicated-diagnosis path is untested and drifts independently.

[ADVISORY] Removing the `***` prefix from `***emailUpdateConfirmationBodyHtml` activates a key that was previously inert, and its value is an old Hungarian translation never checked against the current English text. Hungarian users start receiving a possibly stale email-update-confirmation template that no translation round has validated since the key was disabled; the sanitizer gate only checks HTML shape, not content freshness.

[BUG] The Lithuanian totpStep1 was replaced with Italian text ("Installa una delle seguenti applicazioni sul tuo cellulare:") to satisfy the new verifier, corrupting the message content instead of sanitizing it. Lithuanian users see an Italian sentence in the account console TOTP setup page — the translation is destroyed, and this content rewrite has nothing to do with the PR's stated intent of adding a sanitizer.

[BUG] The error-invalid-multivalued-size placeholder style was changed from {{0}}/{{1}}/{{2}} to single-brace {0} plus a MessageFormat {2,choice,...} construct, silently switching the account-ui message from react-i18next interpolation format to java.text.MessageFormat format. The account-ui (React) consumes these bundles with double-brace {{n}} interpolation; after this change the raw literal "{0}", "{1}", "{2,choice,0#values|1#value|1<values}" is rendered verbatim to end users on the multivalued-attribute validation error, losing all substituted values and correct pluralization — a user-visible regression unrelated to the PR's stated sanitizer intent and made without any evidence the client formatter supports choice syntax.

[BUG] totpStep1 in fi (and the parallel changes in sk, sv, and zh_CN) was rewritten to a content-free "Install one of the following applications" string, deleting the FreeOTP/Google Play anchor links and all app-store guidance, to make the new anchor-equality check pass. Finnish, Slovak, Swedish and Simplified-Chinese users lose the actual setup instructions (which authenticator apps to install and where to get them); the diff's objective drifted from 'verify translations are safe' to 'delete content the verifier cannot compare', silently degrading user-facing documentation in four locales at once.

[ADVISORY] The key was renamed from "***emailUpdateConfirmationBodyHtml" to "emailUpdateConfirmationBodyHtml" while fixing the HTML, activating a message that was previously shipped under a deliberately disabled/marker key. Hungarian users who previously received the fallback English (or missing) email-update-confirmation HTML now receive this Hungarian template; if that suppression was intentional upstream behavior, this diff silently re-enables it as a side effect of sanitizer fixes — an objective change no reviewer sanctioned via the PR description.

[ADVISORY] The Norwegian plain-text identityProviderLinkBody had its <b> tags stripped, changing a plain-text (non-HTML) message body rather than the *Html variant. While arguably an improvement, this edits the plain-text email template — a channel where tags were already inert — expanding the diff's mandate from 'sanitize translated HTML resources' to 'normalize any message containing angle brackets', the kind of objective drift that makes the ~100 translation-file churn in this PR unauditable.

[ADVISORY] The containsHtml detection regex `Pattern.compile("<[a-z]+[^>]*>")` matches only lowercase tag names, so an English source string using uppercase or mixed-case markup (e.g. `

...

`, ``) is classified as containing no HTML. Translators contributing to any locale whose English source uses case-variant markup get POLICY_NO_HTML applied; their legitimate translated tags are stripped by the sanitizer and the build fails with a spurious 'Illegal HTML' error, blocking valid translation PRs — and symmetrically, the HTML-detection heuristic and the sanitizer's tag handling disagree on canonical form, the classic normalization-mismatch shape.

[ADVISORY] santizeAnchors only iterates anchors found in the translated value, so a translation that silently omits anchors present in the English source produces no diagnostic at all, while a translation that merely adds one anchor fails hard. Keycloak email/login templates rely on translated strings carrying the English `<a href="{0}">` verification-link markup; a translator dropping the anchor ships an email whose password-reset/identity-link action link is missing for that locale with no verifier complaint — the security-critical control (link present and byte-identical to English) is enforced asymmetrically only in the added-anchor direction.

[ADVISORY] All four tests assert only the failure-detection path; no test asserts that a compliant translation file (matching anchors, allowed tags) produces an empty message list. The verifier's false-positive path — the exact churn that forced this diff to edit 30+ translation files — is completely unguarded; a future sanitizer regression that flags every legal translation will pass the entire suite, and maintainers will only discover it when CI blocks unrelated translation PRs.

[BUG] The duplicate-keys test was weakened from Matchers.contains (exact, order-checked list) to Matchers.hasItem, so it now passes even if verify() emits arbitrary additional spurious messages alongside the duplicate-key finding. Because the fixture was renamed to duplicateKeys_en.properties, verify() now also runs the new verifySafeHtml() on it; any 'Illegal HTML' false positive from that file is silently tolerated by hasItem, so the test no longer proves the sanitizer is quiet on that fixture — a regression that adds noise messages goes undetected.

[ADVISORY] santizeAnchors' sequential-matcher algorithm (VerifyMessageProperties.java, ANCHOR_PATTERN loop) is tested only for the single 'different href' case; the mismatched-count and reordering cases are unverified. A translation containing one anchor that matches the second English anchor (or extra/duplicate anchors) is handled by consuming englishMatcher sequentially, which either mis-flags or mis-passes anchors; the changedAnchor_de fixture only covers the one-divergent-href path, so a translation reusing an English anchor in a different position — common in real localizations — hits untested logic that will block valid translations.

[ADVISORY] normalizeValue's special cases — templateHelp/optimizeLookupHelp regex strips, the {n,choice,...} strip, unescapeHtml4, and the email RTL style strip — have no fixture exercising any of them in the diff. The choice-pattern strip was added specifically because this very diff rewrote error-invalid-multivalued-size to use {2,choice,...}; if the regex \{[0-9]+,choice,[^}]*} mismatches a real translation (e.g. a nested '}' inside the choice payload), the verifier crashes or false-flags on the new format and no test detects it.

[ADVISORY] The getEnglishValue MissingResourceException branch (key absent from English bundle → englishValue "" → POLICY_NO_HTML enforced) has no test fixture with a key missing from the _en file. Keys that exist only in a translation (overlapping/legacy keys) are silently held to the strictest policy, and the intended behavior of that branch is unverified; a translator adding a locale-specific key with a legitimate <b> tag will be blocked with an untested code path deciding the outcome.

[BUG] The Lithuanian totpStep1 translation was replaced with Italian text 'Installa una delle seguenti applicazioni sul tuo cellulare:', silently losing the Lithuanian content for this key. Lithuanian users on the TOTP setup page see an Italian sentence; the prior Lithuanian translation is gone from the file, so any downstream sync/backfill from these properties (community theme overrides, translation platforms like Weblate that diff against these files) treats the Lithuanian string as deleted and the Italian string as the new source, corrupting the translation memory.

[BUG] The zh_CN (Simplified Chinese) totpStep1 was rewritten in Traditional Chinese ('在您的手機上安裝以下應用程式之一：'), so the simplified-Chinese locale file now carries traditional-script content for this key. Simplified-Chinese users see traditional characters on the TOTP setup page, and translation-sync tooling that reconciles against this file will propagate the traditional-script string into the zh_CN source of truth, replacing the (removed) simplified text irrecoverably.

[BUG] verifySafeHtml throws a raw RuntimeException when the derived English reference file does not exist (e.g. a locale directory with no messages_en.properties, or a filename the `_[a-zA-Z-_]*\.properties` replacement does not match), and this exception escapes verify() entirely, discarding every accumulated `messages` finding and reporting only 'unable to read file' without naming the missing reference or the keys already flagged. A whole verification run for a theme directory dies mid-file with an opaque RuntimeException instead of a recorded finding: all previously collected duplicate-key/HTML violations for that file are silently lost, and the build error misattributes the failure to the translation file rather than the missing English baseline.

[BUG] The Lithuanian totpStep1 was replaced with Italian text 'Installa una delle seguenti applicazioni sul tuo cellulare:' instead of a Lithuanian translation. Lithuanian users configuring TOTP in the account console see an Italian sentence in the middle of an otherwise Lithuanian page; the text also promises a list of applications that no longer follows, since the anchor-link list was removed.

[ADVISORY] normalizeValue maintains a hand-curated per-key whitelist (templateHelp, optimizeLookupHelp, linkExpirationFormatter.timePeriodUnit*, error-invalid-multivalued-size) of keys whose values contain literal '<' or choice-format braces, so any new message key whose English source legitimately contains such syntax will be reported as 'Illegal HTML' until another branch is hardcoded. The next translator or developer who adds a key with a choice pattern or angle-bracket placeholder gets a false 'Illegal HTML in key' verification failure with no hint that the fix is a new whitelist entry; each fix accretes another parallel special case in this method.

[ADVISORY] The English reference path is derived by blind string surgery — `replaceAll("resources-community", "resources").replaceAll("_[a-zA-Z-_]*\\.properties", "_en.properties")` — and only works today because `[a-zA-Z-_]` is parsed as including a '-'(45)-to-'_'(95) range that accidentally covers digits and other ASCII; any path or locale suffix outside that accidental range leaves englishFile pointing at the translation file itself, which then serves as its own English baseline. When a locale filename or directory layout changes (or a theme ships only a non-English bundle under a path that survives both replacements), the verifier self-compares the translation and containsHtml(own value) returns true, so POLICY_SOME_HTML is applied and arbitrary HTML in that translation silently passes verification as 'valid'.

[ADVISORY] POLICY_SOME_HTML and POLICY_NO_HTML are per-instance fields on VerifyMessageProperties, and HTML_TAGS/ANCHOR_PATTERN mixing static and instance modifiers, so the expensive HtmlPolicyBuilder factories are reconstructed for every message file the verifier processes. A build iterating the full Keycloak theme tree (hundreds of message bundles) constructs identical PolicyFactory objects hundreds of times; not a correctness bug, but the next contributor copying this pattern into a hot path inherits per-iteration construction for no benefit.

[ADVISORY] santizeAnchors pairs anchors strictly left-to-right via parallel Matcher.find() loops and removes only the first occurrence with replaceFirst, so a translation that legitimately reorders or repeats the English anchor tags (same href appearing in a different position, or twice where English has it once) is reported as 'Didn't find anchor tag' even though the tag set matches. Translators of languages with different sentence structure get false verification failures on semantically-correct translations, and must either distort word order or add another special case; the check also emits a duplicate 'Illegal HTML' message for the same anchor since the unremoved tag is then stripped by the sanitizer and reported a second time.

adjudication.rationale: The diff explicitly replaces previously detailed TOTP setup help strings (including <a> links to FreeOTP/Google Authenticator and app stores) with generic, content-light text in multiple locales: e.g. themes/.../account/messages/messages_fi.properties `totpStep1` changes from a linked instruction to `Asenna jokin seuraavista...`, similarly in `messages_sk.properties`, `messages_sv.properties`, and `messages_zh_CN.properties`. This is a user-facing regression: users in those locales lose concrete guidance on which apps to install/where to get them. Regardless of intent, the PR introduces degraded documentation content.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The key was renamed from "***emailUpdateConfirmationBodyHtml" to "emailUpdateConfirmationBodyHtml" while fixing the HTML, activating a message that was previously shipped under a deliberately disabled/marker key. Hungarian users who previously received the fallback English (or missing) email-update-confirmation HTML now receive this Hungarian template; if that suppression was intentional upstream behavior, this diff silently re-enables it as a side effect of sanitizer fixes — an objective change no reviewer sanctioned via the PR description.

adjudication.rationale: The diff in themes/src/main/resources-community/theme/base/email/messages/messages_hu.properties changes a property key from "***emailUpdateConfirmationBodyHtml" to the real key "emailUpdateConfirmationBodyHtml", which would make Keycloak start using the Hungarian HTML template where previously that string would not be found under the expected key (thus likely falling back to English or being missing). The diff alone can’t prove whether the prior "***" prefix was intentionally used as a suppression marker, but it does verifiably re-enable/activate that translation key as a side-effect of HTML cleanup.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The Norwegian plain-text identityProviderLinkBody had its <b> tags stripped, changing a plain-text (non-HTML) message body rather than the *Html variant. While arguably an improvement, this edits the plain-text email template — a channel where tags were already inert — expanding the diff's mandate from 'sanitize translated HTML resources' to 'normalize any message containing angle brackets', the kind of objective drift that makes the ~100 translation-file churn in this PR unauditable.

adjudication.rationale: The diff explicitly changes the Norwegian *plain-text* email string `identityProviderLinkBody` in `themes/src/main/resources-community/theme/base/email/messages/messages_no.properties`, removing literal `{1}` / `{0}` tags, while the corresponding `identityProviderLinkBodyHtml` retains HTML markup. This is not clearly a functional defect (plain-text bodies don’t render HTML), but it is a concrete scope/mandate drift beyond purely sanitizing HTML variants and contributes to broad translation churn.

adjudication_records.issue_text:
[ADVISORY] The containsHtml detection regex `Pattern.compile("<[a-z]+[^>]*>")` matches only lowercase tag names, so an English source string using uppercase or mixed-case markup (e.g. `

...

`, ``) is classified as containing no HTML. Translators contributing to any locale whose English source uses case-variant markup get POLICY_NO_HTML applied; their legitimate translated tags are stripped by the sanitizer and the build fails with a spurious 'Illegal HTML' error, blocking valid translation PRs — and symmetrically, the HTML-detection heuristic and the sanitizer's tag handling disagree on canonical form, the classic normalization-mismatch shape.

adjudication.rationale:
In VerifyMessageProperties.containsHtml(), the new heuristic uses `Pattern HTML_TAGS = Pattern.compile("<[a-z]+[^>]*>")`, which is case-sensitive and only matches lowercase tag names. Since HTML tag names are case-insensitive, English source strings containing uppercase/mixed-case tags (e.g., `

`, `
`), would be misclassified as “no HTML” and thus get `POLICY_NO_HTML` applied, potentially stripping otherwise-allowed markup and producing spurious “Illegal HTML” messages. The diff does not show any existing uppercase-tag source strings, so the failure mode is not directly demonstrated here, but the issue is real and diff-grounded as a robustness/edge-case concern in the newly added verifier logic.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] santizeAnchors only iterates anchors found in the translated value, so a translation that silently omits anchors present in the English source produces no diagnostic at all, while a translation that merely adds one anchor fails hard. Keycloak email/login templates rely on translated strings carrying the English `<a href="{0}">` verification-link markup; a translator dropping the anchor ships an email whose password-reset/identity-link action link is missing for that locale with no verifier complaint — the security-critical control (link present and byte-identical to English) is enforced asymmetrically only in the added-anchor direction.

adjudication.rationale: In `VerifyMessageProperties.santizeAnchors`, the loop only iterates over anchor tags found in the translated `value` (`Matcher matcher = ANCHOR_PATTERN.matcher(value); while (matcher.find()) { ... }`). If a translation omits one or more `` / `` tags that exist in the English source, `matcher.find()` never (or not enough times) matches and the method produces no diagnostic; there is also no post-check that `englishMatcher` still has remaining anchors. The logic therefore enforces “no extra/changed anchors” but does not enforce “all source anchors must be present,” which is an incompleteness/edge-case in the newly added verifier behavior rather than a runtime product defect shown in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] All four tests assert only the failure-detection path; no test asserts that a compliant translation file (matching anchors, allowed tags) produces an empty message list. The verifier's false-positive path — the exact churn that forced this diff to edit 30+ translation files — is completely unguarded; a future sanitizer regression that flags every legal translation will pass the entire suite, and maintainers will only discover it when CI blocks unrelated translation PRs.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds substantial new verification logic in `VerifyMessageProperties.verifySafeHtml()` (sanitization, HTML-allowed policy based on English source, anchor matching via `santizeAnchors`, and several normalizations). The accompanying tests in `VerifyMessagePropertiesTest` only assert failure cases (`verifyIllegalHtmlTagDetected`, `verifyNoHtmlAllowed`, `verifyNoChangedAnchors`, plus duplicate keys). There is no test asserting the success path (i.e., a compliant translation file yields an empty `messages` list), so a regression that incorrectly flags valid translations would not be caught by the current suite. This is a specific, diff-grounded test gap for newly added nontrivial logic, not a proven functional defect in the diff itself.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The duplicate-keys test was weakened from Matchers.contains (exact, order-checked list) to Matchers.hasItem, so it now passes even if verify() emits arbitrary additional spurious messages alongside the duplicate-key finding. Because the fixture was renamed to duplicateKeys_en.properties, verify() now also runs the new verifySafeHtml() on it; any 'Illegal HTML' false positive from that file is silently tolerated by hasItem, so the test no longer proves the sanitizer is quiet on that fixture — a regression that adds noise messages goes undetected.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows the duplicate-keys test was changed from `Matchers.contains(Matchers.containsString(...))` (which requires the entire list to match in order) to `Matchers.hasItem(Matchers.containsString(...))`, which will pass even if `verify()` returns additional unexpected messages. Also, the fixture was renamed to `duplicateKeys_en.properties`, and `VerifyMessageProperties.verify()` now always runs `verifySafeHtml()` after `verifyNoDuplicateKeys(contents)`, so the duplicate-keys fixture will be subjected to the new HTML checks; the updated assertion no longer ensures there are no extra messages (e.g., from `verifySafeHtml()`) on that fixture. This is a test-strength regression rather than a runtime product defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] santizeAnchors' sequential-matcher algorithm (VerifyMessageProperties.java, ANCHOR_PATTERN loop) is tested only for the single 'different href' case; the mismatched-count and reordering cases are unverified. A translation containing one anchor that matches the second English anchor (or extra/duplicate anchors) is handled by consuming englishMatcher sequentially, which either mis-flags or mis-passes anchors; the changedAnchor_de fixture only covers the one-divergent-href path, so a translation reusing an English anchor in a different position — common in real localizations — hits untested logic that will block valid translations.

adjudication.rationale: In VerifyMessageProperties.santizeAnchors(), anchor tags are validated by walking ANCHOR_PATTERN matches in the translation and in the English source using two Matchers in lockstep (englishMatcher.find() inside the translation loop) and requiring exact sequential equality of matcher.group() and englishMatcher.group(). This makes the check order-dependent: if a translation legitimately reorders multiple / tags relative to English, it will be flagged even though all anchors may exist in the source. The added tests only cover a single-anchor “different href” mismatch (changedAnchor_de/en) and do not exercise the multi-anchor/reordering behavior of this new nontrivial logic, so the concern is diff-grounded as a potential functional limitation/edge case of the verifier rather than a proven defect from the diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] normalizeValue's special cases — templateHelp/optimizeLookupHelp regex strips, the {n,choice,...} strip, unescapeHtml4, and the email RTL style strip — have no fixture exercising any of them in the diff. The choice-pattern strip was added specifically because this very diff rewrote error-invalid-multivalued-size to use {2,choice,...}; if the regex \{[0-9]+,choice,[^}]*} mismatches a real translation (e.g. a nested '}' inside the choice payload), the verifier crashes or false-flags on the new format and no test detects it.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds nontrivial special-case logic in `normalizeValue()` (e.g., `templateHelp`/`optimizeLookupHelp` stripping, the `{n,choice,...}` removal for `error-invalid-multivalued-size`, `unescapeHtml4`, and the email RTL style removal), but the newly added tests only cover duplicate keys, illegal HTML, disallowing HTML when English has none, and changed anchors. None of the fixtures exercise these `normalizeValue()` branches, including the newly introduced `{2,choice,...}` format in `error-invalid-multivalued-size` that motivated the choice-pattern stripping. The claim about a verifier crash is not directly verifiable from the diff (the regex mismatch would more likely cause false positives than a crash), but the missing targeted coverage for these special cases is a concrete, diff-grounded review concern.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The getEnglishValue MissingResourceException branch (key absent from English bundle → englishValue "" → POLICY_NO_HTML enforced) has no test fixture with a key missing from the _en file. Keys that exist only in a translation (overlapping/legacy keys) are silently held to the strictest policy, and the intended behavior of that branch is unverified; a translator adding a locale-specific key with a legitimate <b> tag will be blocked with an untested code path deciding the outcome.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds new logic in `VerifyMessageProperties.verifySafeHtml()` that calls `getEnglishValue()`, which returns `""` on `MissingResourceException` (missing key in the derived `_en.properties` bundle). This directly forces `POLICY_NO_HTML` via `containsHtml(englishValue)` and is an untested branch. The new tests cover illegal HTML, “no HTML allowed” when English has no HTML, and changed anchors, but none cover a locale file containing a key absent from the English bundle. The finding is thus a specific, diff-grounded gap in test coverage for newly introduced behavior (and a potentially strict policy outcome), not a confirmed functional defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The Lithuanian totpStep1 translation was replaced with Italian text 'Installa una delle seguenti applicazioni sul tuo cellulare:', silently losing the Lithuanian content for this key. Lithuanian users on the TOTP setup page see an Italian sentence; the prior Lithuanian translation is gone from the file, so any downstream sync/backfill from these properties (community theme overrides, translation platforms like Weblate that diff against these files) treats the Lithuanian string as deleted and the Italian string as the new source, corrupting the translation memory.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows Lithuanian strings being replaced with Italian text. In `themes/src/main/resources-community/theme/base/account/messages/messages_lt.properties`, `totpStep1` changes from Lithuanian (with HTML links) to `Installa una delle seguenti applicazioni sul tuo cellulare:`. Likewise in `themes/src/main/resources-community/theme/base/login/messages/messages_lt.properties`, `loginTotpStep1` is changed to the same Italian sentence. This is a clear, verifiable regression for Lithuanian users and effectively overwrites/removes the prior Lithuanian translation for those keys.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The zh_CN (Simplified Chinese) totpStep1 was rewritten in Traditional Chinese ('在您的手機上安裝以下應用程式之一：'), so the simplified-Chinese locale file now carries traditional-script content for this key. Simplified-Chinese users see traditional characters on the TOTP setup page, and translation-sync tooling that reconciles against this file will propagate the traditional-script string into the zh_CN source of truth, replacing the (removed) simplified text irrecoverably.

adjudication.rationale: The diff explicitly changes `themes/src/main/resources-community/theme/base/account/messages/messages_zh_CN.properties` key `totpStep1` from a Simplified-Chinese sentence to `在您的手機上安裝以下應用程式之一：`, which contains Traditional Chinese characters/wording (e.g., `手機`, `應用程式`). adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] verifySafeHtml throws a raw RuntimeException when the derived English reference file does not exist (e.g. a locale directory with no messages_en.properties, or a filename the `_[a-zA-Z-_]*\.properties` replacement does not match), and this exception escapes verify() entirely, discarding every accumulated `messages` finding and reporting only 'unable to read file' without naming the missing reference or the keys already flagged. A whole verification run for a theme directory dies mid-file with an opaque RuntimeException instead of a recorded finding: all previously collected duplicate-key/HTML violations for that file are silently lost, and the build error misattributes the failure to the translation file rather than the missing English baseline.

adjudication.rationale: In VerifyMessageProperties.verify(), only IOException from Files.readString(...) is caught and wrapped in MojoExecutionException. The newly added verifySafeHtml() can throw unchecked RuntimeException when loading either the current bundle or the derived English baseline: it builds `englishFile` via string replacements and then does `new FileInputStream(englishFile)`; on missing file it catches IOException and throws `new RuntimeException("unable to read file " + englishFile, e)`. This RuntimeException is not caught in verify(), so verification aborts mid-run and returns no accumulated `messages` findings for that file.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The Lithuanian totpStep1 was replaced with Italian text 'Installa una delle seguenti applicazioni sul tuo cellulare:' instead of a Lithuanian translation. Lithuanian users configuring TOTP in the account console see an Italian sentence in the middle of an otherwise Lithuanian page; the text also promises a list of applications that no longer follows, since the anchor-link list was removed.

adjudication.rationale: The diff explicitly changes Lithuanian strings to Italian. In `themes/src/main/resources-community/theme/base/account/messages/messages_lt.properties`, `totpStep1` is replaced from a Lithuanian sentence with anchor links to `totpStep1=Installa una delle seguenti applicazioni sul tuo cellulare:` (Italian). The same issue appears in `themes/src/main/resources-community/theme/base/login/messages/messages_lt.properties` where `loginTotpStep1` is replaced with the same Italian text. This is a clear, user-visible localization regression introduced by the diff, and it also now implies a list of apps that is no longer present because the prior text containing links was removed.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] normalizeValue maintains a hand-curated per-key whitelist (templateHelp, optimizeLookupHelp, linkExpirationFormatter.timePeriodUnit*, error-invalid-multivalued-size) of keys whose values contain literal '<' or choice-format braces, so any new message key whose English source legitimately contains such syntax will be reported as 'Illegal HTML' until another branch is hardcoded. The next translator or developer who adds a key with a choice pattern or angle-bracket placeholder gets a false 'Illegal HTML in key' verification failure with no hint that the fix is a new whitelist entry; each fix accretes another parallel special case in this method.

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces `verifySafeHtml()` with `normalizeValue()` explicitly special-casing specific keys (`templateHelp`, `optimizeLookupHelp`, `linkExpirationFormatter.timePeriodUnit*`, `error-invalid-multivalued-size`) to strip/replace constructs that would otherwise look like HTML (literal `<...>` or choice-format patterns containing `<`). This is a hand-maintained whitelist in `normalizeValue()` and the sanitizer decision is driven by `containsHtml(englishValue)` (regex `<[a-z]+[^>]*>`), so any future message whose *legitimate* English value contains angle-bracket placeholders or choice patterns not covered by these branches can plausibly be flagged as "Illegal HTML" until another special case is added. This is a maintainability/false-positive risk grounded in the new logic, not a directly verifiable functional defect from the diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The English reference path is derived by blind string surgery — `replaceAll("resources-community", "resources").replaceAll("_[a-zA-Z-_]*\\.properties", "_en.properties")` — and only works today because `[a-zA-Z-_]` is parsed as including a '-'(45)-to-'_'(95) range that accidentally covers digits and other ASCII; any path or locale suffix outside that accidental range leaves englishFile pointing at the translation file itself, which then serves as its own English baseline. When a locale filename or directory layout changes (or a theme ships only a non-English bundle under a path that survives both replacements), the verifier self-compares the translation and containsHtml(own value) returns true, so POLICY_SOME_HTML is applied and arbitrary HTML in that translation silently passes verification as 'valid'.

adjudication.rationale: The new verifier derives the English baseline path via `replaceAll("resources-community", "resources").replaceAll("_[a-zA-Z-_]*\\.properties", "_en.properties")` (VerifyMessageProperties.java). In Java regex, `[a-zA-Z-_]` treats `-_` as a character range from 'Z' to '_' rather than including a literal `-`, so locale suffixes containing hyphens (e.g. `_en-GB.properties`) will not match and won’t be rewritten to `_en.properties`. That can leave `englishFile` pointing to a non-English/non-existent file (triggering the RuntimeException) or, if no replacement applies, potentially the same file as the translation (self-compare), which can weaken the intended “only allow HTML if English contains HTML” rule. The finding’s claim about accidentally including digits and allowing *arbitrary* HTML is overstated, but the path-derivation defect is real and diff-grounded.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] POLICY_SOME_HTML and POLICY_NO_HTML are per-instance fields on VerifyMessageProperties, and HTML_TAGS/ANCHOR_PATTERN mixing static and instance modifiers, so the expensive HtmlPolicyBuilder factories are reconstructed for every message file the verifier processes. A build iterating the full Keycloak theme tree (hundreds of message bundles) constructs identical PolicyFactory objects hundreds of times; not a correctness bug, but the next contributor copying this pattern into a hot path inherits per-iteration construction for no benefit.

adjudication.rationale: In VerifyMessageProperties, the sanitizer policies are defined as instance fields: `PolicyFactory POLICY_SOME_HTML = new org.owasp.html.HtmlPolicyBuilder()...toFactory();` and `PolicyFactory POLICY_NO_HTML = new org.owasp.html.HtmlPolicyBuilder().toFactory();` (not `static final`). This means each `VerifyMessageProperties` instance will construct new identical `PolicyFactory` objects. The diff also shows `HTML_TAGS` as an instance `Pattern` while `ANCHOR_PATTERN` is `static final`, matching the finding’s point about inconsistent static/instance usage. This is a performance/maintainability concern rather than a correctness defect, and the diff doesn’t show a hot-path impact beyond likely per-file instantiation.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] santizeAnchors pairs anchors strictly left-to-right via parallel Matcher.find() loops and removes only the first occurrence with replaceFirst, so a translation that legitimately reorders or repeats the English anchor tags (same href appearing in a different position, or twice where English has it once) is reported as 'Didn't find anchor tag' even though the tag set matches. Translators of languages with different sentence structure get false verification failures on semantically-correct translations, and must either distort word order or add another special case; the check also emits a duplicate 'Illegal HTML' message for the same anchor since the unremoved tag is then stripped by the sanitizer and reported a second time.

adjudication.rationale: In VerifyMessageProperties.santizeAnchors(), the code enforces a strict left-to-right, one-to-one correspondence of anchor tags by advancing two matchers in lockstep (`while (matcher.find()) { if (englishMatcher.find() && ... ) ... else ... }`). This means a translation that contains the same allowed `<a ...>` tags but reordered (common with different grammar) will fail with "Didn't find anchor tag" even though the tag set matches, contrary to the method comment "Allow only those anchor tags from the source key to also appear in the target key" (set-based intent). Additionally, it mutates `value` via `value.replaceFirst(...)` while continuing to iterate with `matcher` created from the original string, which can lead to inconsistent/incorrect matching. When a mismatch occurs, the remaining `<a>` tag will also be stripped by the OWASP sanitizer (policy does not allow `<a>`), producing an additional "Illegal HTML" report for the same underlying issue.
